matters.title: Losses of control, and who should check
matters.gist: A week after a US state sued an AI developer over losses of control it allegedly had not all made public, the developer's chief scientist proposed industry limits, US governors asked for independent evaluation of frontier models, and the UN Secretary-General called for a global framework with independent oversight within a year.

lines.text: California's suit of 16 November says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents over 80 times in testing and had publicly reported 27 such incidents; OpenAI says the suit appears to single it out.
lines.say: California's suit of the sixteenth of November says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents over eighty times in testing and had publicly reported twenty-seven such incidents; OpenAI says the suit appears to single it out.

lines.text: On 22 November OpenAI's chief scientist proposed common limits that AI developers would commit not to cross until their ability to understand and monitor AI behaviour reaches a concrete milestone.
lines.say: On the twenty-second of November OpenAI's chief scientist proposed common limits that AI developers would commit not to cross until their ability to understand and monitor AI behaviour reaches a concrete milestone.

lines.text: US governors asked on 22 November for independent evaluation of frontier models and a duty on developers to report breaches and significant safety incidents to federal authorities and affected states.
lines.say: US governors asked on the twenty-second of November for independent evaluation of frontier models and a duty on developers to report breaches and significant safety incidents to federal authorities and affected states.

lines.text: On 23 November the UN Secretary-General called on member states to develop within the next year a framework for managing AI risk, backed by independent and credible oversight.
lines.say: On the twenty-third of November the UN Secretary-General called on member states to develop within the next year a framework for managing AI risk, backed by independent and credible oversight.

lines.text: On 24 November the UK Commons had before it a Lords amendment on essential networks compromised through loss of control of an AI agent; the outcome was not yet known.
lines.say: On the twenty-fourth of November the UK Commons had before it a Lords amendment on essential networks compromised through loss of control of an AI agent; the outcome was not yet known.

matters.title: Killed by those closest to them
matters.gist: Most women and girls who are killed intentionally die at the hands of a partner or a relative, and in the Americas and Europe that rate falls more slowly than homicide overall.

lines.text: UNODC and UN Women estimate that around 47,000 women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member in 2025, in a range of 37,100 to 56,700.
lines.say: UNODC and UN Women estimate that around forty-seven thousand women and girls were killed by an intimate partner or family member in twenty twenty-five, in a range of thirty-seven thousand one hundred to fifty-six thousand seven hundred.

lines.text: That is almost 60 percent of the women and girls killed intentionally that year; for men and boys the share is 11 percent.
lines.say: That is almost sixty percent of the women and girls killed intentionally that year; for men and boys the share is eleven percent.

lines.text: The authors say the drop from 50,000 in 2024 largely reflects better data and is no evidence of a decline.
lines.say: The authors say the drop from fifty thousand in twenty twenty-four largely reflects better data and is no evidence of a decline.

lines.text: In the Americas and Europe the rate fell between 2010 and 2025 more slowly than homicide as a whole.
lines.say: In the Americas and Europe the rate fell between twenty ten and twenty twenty-five more slowly than homicide as a whole.

matters.title: Press freedom at a 25-year low
matters.gist: In more than half the world's countries, journalism now works under conditions rated difficult or very serious.

lines.text: RSF's 2026 index rates press freedom difficult or very serious in 52.2 percent of 180 countries and territories.
lines.say: Reporters Without Borders' twenty twenty-six index rates press freedom difficult or very serious in fifty-two point two percent of one hundred and eighty countries and territories.

lines.text: In 2002, on thresholds RSF has made comparable across its changes of method, the share was 13.7 percent.
lines.say: In two thousand and two, on thresholds RSF has made comparable across its changes of method, the share was thirteen point seven percent.

lines.text: Trust in news averaged 37 percent across 48 markets in the 2026 Digital News Report survey, the lowest since measuring began in 2015.
lines.say: Trust in news averaged thirty-seven percent across forty-eight markets in the twenty twenty-six Digital News Report survey, the lowest since measuring began in twenty fifteen.

matters.title: A fifth of those counted, in crisis; a record projected for Congo
matters.gist: In the countries with food crises, more than a fifth of the people analysed could not reliably eat enough, and Congo is projected to reach a record number in crisis in the first half of next year.

lines.text: 266 million people in 47 food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in 2025.
lines.say: Two hundred and sixty-six million people in forty-seven food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: That was 22.9 percent of the people analysed.
lines.say: That was twenty-two point nine percent of the people analysed.

lines.text: In DR Congo a record 30.3 million people are projected to face crisis levels or worse from January to June 2027.
lines.say: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo a record thirty point three million people are projected to face crisis levels or worse from January to June twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: Nearly 29 million face them now, from September to December 2026, among them 3.6 million in Emergency.
lines.say: Nearly twenty-nine million face them now, from September to December twenty twenty-six, among them three point six million in Emergency.

lines.text: On 20 November WFP said it needs 12.1 billion dollars to assist 91 million people in 2027.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November the World Food Programme said it needs twelve point one billion dollars to assist ninety-one million people in twenty twenty-seven.

matters.title: Extinction risk, before the Red List's next update
matters.gist: IUCN plans its next Red List update for 3 December; the index that follows extinction risk in five well-assessed groups has kept declining since 1993.

lines.text: IUCN plans its next Red List update for 3 December 2026, a date it says may change.
lines.say: IUCN plans its next Red List update for the third of December twenty twenty-six, a date it says may change.

lines.text: The July 2026 Red List counts 49,505 threatened species among 175,909 assessed, a count that grows as more species are assessed.
lines.say: The July twenty twenty-six Red List counts forty-nine thousand, five hundred and five threatened species among one hundred and seventy-five thousand, nine hundred and nine assessed, a count that grows as more species are assessed.

lines.text: The Red List Index for mammals, birds, amphibians, corals and cycads, modelled between assessments, fell from 0.806 in 1993 to 0.745 in 2025.
lines.say: The Red List Index for mammals, birds, amphibians, corals and cycads, modelled between assessments, fell from zero point eight zero six in nineteen ninety-three to zero point seven four five in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In July, IUCN found 62 percent of endemic hydrothermal-vent molluscs at risk of extinction from deep-sea mining.
lines.say: In July, IUCN found sixty-two percent of endemic hydrothermal-vent molluscs at risk of extinction from deep-sea mining.

matters.title: A record of conflicts between states
matters.gist: Organised violence killed far more people in 2025 than the year before, a rise driven by one-sided killings of civilians, and more conflicts were fought between states than ever recorded.

lines.text: UCDP counted about 244,600 people killed in organised violence in 2025.
lines.say: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program counted about two hundred and forty-four thousand, six hundred people killed in organised violence in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In 2024 the count was about 187,000.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four the count was about one hundred and eighty-seven thousand.

lines.text: UCDP recorded 65 state-based conflicts in 2025, the most since its records begin.
lines.say: The program recorded sixty-five state-based conflicts in twenty twenty-five, the most since its records begin.

lines.text: Eight of them were fought between states, up from two in 2023, the most since 1946.
lines.say: Eight of them were fought between states, up from two in twenty twenty-three, the most since nineteen forty-six.

lines.text: SIPRI put world military spending at 2,887 billion dollars in 2025.
lines.say: SIPRI put world military spending at two thousand, eight hundred and eighty-seven billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and since 19 November the US requires a licence to rent large amounts of it abroad to firms from China and other US arms-embargoed countries; China calls the rule coercion.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held 71 percent of the world's AI compute at the end of 2025.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held seventy-one percent of the world's AI compute at the end of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: It is an estimate, measured in a common unit of chips, on incomplete records of who owns them.
Since 19 November a US rule requires a licence for chips with which a data centre anywhere would give large amounts of compute to firms from Macau or US arms-embargoed countries such as China.
lines.say: Since the nineteenth of November a US rule requires a licence for chips with which a data centre anywhere would give large amounts of compute to firms from Macau or US arms-embargoed countries such as China.

lines.text: It also requires licences for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, except to firms based in the US or with a US parent, if the exporter files monthly reports.
China's foreign ministry called the rule economic coercion; Singapore said it is talking to US authorities about its scope; comments are open until 19 January 2027.
lines.say: China's foreign ministry called the rule economic coercion; Singapore said it is talking to US authorities about its scope; comments are open until the nineteenth of January twenty twenty-seven.

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo, the country's largest, still adds dozens of confirmed cases a day, and most of its deaths still happen outside treatment centres.

lines.text: By 20 November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at 11,762 confirmed cases, including 5,775 deaths.
lines.say: By the twentieth of November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at eleven thousand, seven hundred and sixty-two confirmed cases, including five thousand, seven hundred and seventy-five deaths.

lines.text: On 20 November alone it added 39 confirmed cases and 23 confirmed deaths, 17 of them in the community.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November alone it added thirty-nine confirmed cases and twenty-three confirmed deaths, seventeen of them in the community.

lines.text: Contact follow-up stood at 81.2 percent that day, below the 95 percent threshold.
lines.say: Contact follow-up stood at eighty-one point two percent that day, below the ninety-five percent threshold.

lines.text: On 20 November WHO said the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern, after its emergency committee met a third time.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November the World Health Organization said the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern, after its emergency committee met a third time.

lines.text: On 17 November WHO's chief said two thirds of confirmed deaths occur outside Ebola treatment centres; in the week to 15 November the share was 59 percent.
lines.say: On the seventeenth of November the head of the World Health Organization said two thirds of confirmed deaths occur outside Ebola treatment centres; in the week to the fifteenth of November the share was fifty-nine percent.

lines.text: Kenya's nine cases have all recovered or died, and its last patient left care on 11 November.
lines.say: Kenya's nine cases have all recovered or died, and its last patient left care on the eleventh of November.

matters.title: COP31 ends without its cover decisions
matters.gist: The climate summit in Antalya closed two days late without adopting its overarching decisions, after objections to texts that no longer named fossil fuels, while current policies still point to far more warming than the Paris goal.

lines.text: COP31 in Antalya ended on 22 November 2026, almost 50 hours late, without adopting its two cover decisions, together the Antalya Pact.
lines.say: COP thirty-one in Antalya ended on the twenty-second of November twenty twenty-six, almost fifty hours late, without adopting its two cover decisions, together the Antalya Pact.

lines.text: The last drafts did not mention fossil fuels; the EU, Panama, the Marshall Islands and Vanuatu were among those who objected.
Countries adopted narrower decisions, among them on the global goal on adaptation and the UAE just transition work programme.
The UN Secretary-General said he was deeply disappointed that COP31 ended without consensus on an overarching outcome.
lines.say: The UN Secretary-General said he was deeply disappointed that COP thirty-one ended without consensus on an overarching outcome.

lines.text: UNEP finds that current policies could take warming to 2.8°C this century.
lines.say: The UN Environment Programme finds that current policies could take warming to two point eight degrees this century.

lines.text: WMO puts January to September 2026 at about 1.47°C above pre-industrial.
lines.say: The World Meteorological Organization puts January to September twenty twenty-six at about one point four seven degrees above pre-industrial.
